newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikkei ends up two pct on settlements, buy-backs.
newsitem.headline: Nikkei ends up two pct on settlements, buy-backs.

text.p: The Nikkei 225 stock average ended more than two percent higher on Friday, bolstered by options settlements in the morning and buy-backs in the banking sector in the afternoon, brokers said.
The Nikkei closed up 361.23 points, or 2.07 percent, at 17,846.98. Its June futures ended 340 points higher at 17,830 points.

"The Nikkei average ended feebly on Thursday, but losses were limited today, even with the April options settlement, which had more buy than sell positions, contrary to expectations," said Toyo Securities director Haruo Nakaharu.
"The limited losses encouraged market participants to buy-back bank shares, which had been sold off heavily recently, ahead of the weekend," Nakaharu added.
Turnover totalled 485 million shares, down from 497 million on Thursday. Gainers outpaced declining issues 666 to 439, while 143 were unchanged.

Other indices were mostly higher, with TOPIX up 15.71 points, or 1.19 percent, at 1,336.53. The Nikkei 300 added 2.94 points, or 1.15 percent, to end at 259.67. The second-section index however, slipped 12.69 points, or 0.82 percent, to 1,527.31.
Turnover was 8.54 million shares, down slightly from 7.88 million traded on Thursday. The over-the-counter index had shed 5.03 points, or 0.47 percent, to 1,054.60 by late Tokyo.

Brokers said that apart from a spreading view that investors after bargains were prowling below the 17,500 psychological threshold, preventing sharp falls, Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) shares played a large part in fueling the rally seen late in the day.
NCB hit its limit high in the afternoon after its announcement on Thursday that it plans to its tie up with Bankers Trust New York Corp.

"It was mostly margin-trade related short covering today, but somewhere along the way, investors may gradually start to commend the (tie-up) move as it means there is one less possible factor to upset Japan's financial system," said Akishige Ishikura, an analyst at Dai-Ichi Securities.
The shares ended at 240, up a maximum 50 yen, or 26.32 percent.
A total of 24.96 million NCB shares were traded. It was both the largest percentage gainer and the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse for a second straight session.

The second most heavily traded issue, with 7.68 million shares changing hands, was Sakura Bank Ltd. It edged up five yen to end at 610, successfully recovering from a fit of weakness which brought it down to a low of 585.
Weakness in most bank shares in the morning dragged the Nikkei to a low of 17,447,64, but the sector was later boosted by the NCB rally, which helped pushed the index higher.
Sumitomo Bank Ltd ended up 30 yen at 1,220.
Export-strong issues were mixed. Recent high-flyers such as TDK Corp, which were bought on the back of a weakening yen, fell prey to profit taking. It lost 110 yen to 8,930.

However, recent laggards such as Hitachi Ltd added 30 yen to 1,150. NEC Corp rose 10 yen to 1,520. "The yen is weak against the dollar which is definitely a plus for exporters," said Nakaharu. "But investors are starting to trade exporter issues based on technical factors rather than the weak yen, so some are being bought and others sold."

Brokers added that buying began to spread to low-priced, domestic-demand sensitive issues, such as steel and chemicals and this was likely to continue next week. Kawasaki Steel Corp added two yen to 357. On a sector basis, major losses were posted only by credit/lease and land transport.
The advancing sectors were led by transportation equipment, mining, warehousing, railway/bus and fisheries.
Brokers said the rise above 17,500 and the sharply higher close meant market sentiment was somewhat brighter.

They said it was still possible that pessimism in bad-loan affected sectors could force the index down again next week to near its January 10 year-low of 17,303, but such slumps were likely to be brief and rescued by bargain-hunting pension funds.
-- Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9052
